newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Listless amid crude losses.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Listless amid crude losses.

text.p: Sentiment in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market was weak on Wednesday, reflecting falls in crude values, traders said.
A major was heard lowering its offer for a 180-cst cargo for late June/early July lifting to $102.00 per tonne while a bid was seen at $101.00 for late June delivery, traders said.
The 180-cst grade has been locked within a narrow $101-$103 range since last week.
Traders said demand and supply could be balanced in the near term, with at least five cargoes expected to arrive from the Middle East and the Mediterranean in mid-June.

"Losses in crude values hurt sentiment a little today, but the market should be supported," said one trader, noting recent purchase support from a local trader who had been buying regularly in the past few weeks.
The trader had bought at least five cargoes.
The market is waiting for Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) to announce results of its import tender for two 38,000-tonne July cargoes. The tender closed late today.
CPC last bought two fuel oil cargoes at around $124 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.
The fuel oil swaps market also followed weak crude values. June swaps were quoted at $100.75/$101.50 against Tuesday's $101.00/$101.50 and July swaps slipped to $99.25/$100.00 from $100.00/$100.50.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract, sentiment remained bearish with no transaction reported on late Wednesday.
July contract was bid/offered at $99.00/$100.50 and August was at $98.50/$100.00.
The low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market is awaiting Japan's summer demand to emerge and help digest supplies, which stood at $3.1 million in June from Indonesia.
Traders said LSWR prices, which have been weak in the past few months, might not weaken further as Japan's demand is widely expected to emerge in June for the summer season.
Market focus was also on an import tender from the Korean Electric Power Company (KEPCO), which closes on Thursday.
KEPCO is expected to announce later this week results of the tender for 500,000-barrel cargo for July 18-22 delivery.
